findings.title: Error-handling test asserts no commit, contradicting its docstring and the offset-commit design
findings.description: The docstring says "errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages", and the sibling tests expect a commit after successful processing. The first processing call raises, but `OrderedQueueWorker.run` catches the exception and still calls `complete_offset` in `finally`. Offset 101 should therefore be committable, and `committed_offsets[test_partition]` should be 102. The final assertion instead requires that `test_partition` is absent, or that `committed_offsets` is empty. That passes when no commit happens at all, so the test does not verify the behavior it describes. The assertion should check for the committed value (102) after the failure.

findings.title: Immediate `total_items > 0` assertion races with worker threads
findings.description: The test submits 10 items to a pool whose workers are already running, then immediately asserts `stats["total_items"] > 0`. Workers can drain the queues before `get_stats()` runs, so the count can be 0 and the test can fail intermittently. The assertion should either be removed or made deterministic, for example by blocking the result processor on an event before reading the stats.
